content:
There's no canonical way to refer to the order of a SimpleGraph (its number of vertices). Across the SimpleGraph hierarchy I count 40+ Fintype.card, four Nat.card, and five ENat.card. The ENat.card sites are all paired with ℕ∞-valued companions (chromaticNumber, vertexCoverNum, encard) or use cardinality as a bound where ⊤ ≰ n actively rules out the infinite case.

The other ≈45 sites could consolidate. Would that be worth it? If so, two questions:

1. Body. Fintype.card is zero-import. Nat.card matches mathlib's broader direction but costs one import Mathlib.SetTheory.Cardinal.Finite in Basic.lean and more proof churn.
2. Reducibility. I'd lean abbrevso existing proofs carry through via reducibility, the wrapper is mostly there to give the textbook noun a name. @[expose] def survives in goals but needs one-token nudges at each rw whose pattern targeted Fintype.card V specifically.

Same question applies to the size of a graph, though G.edgeSet.ncard would need Mathlib.Data.Set.Card, a noisier cascade than the order import. Should presumably be a separate PR either way.

These are separate things. Fintype.card requires Fintype (which is generally annoying, and requires a finite graph), and Nat.card doesn't say anything about infinite graphs (as opposed to ENat.card).

Generally I support switching everything to ENat.card/Set.encard (or even Cardinal.mk), but I think it's best to have multiple versions rather than only ENat.card, since it's useful to have Nat inequalities.

Christoph Spiegel said:

though G.edgeSet.ncard would need Mathlib.Data.Set.Card, a noisier cascade than the order import

This is indeed a problem, but now that the simpNF of Fintype.card s is s.ncard (#39414) I hoped we could import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card in SimpleGraph/Basic or SimpleGraph/Finite

Also if you want to add defs/abbrevs for the order of a graph, I'd wait for the vertex-sets refactor, since I don't think it makes sense to define something on G : SimpleGraph V which only depends on V.
I'm not sure we should have defs/abbrevs since G.verts.ncard/G.verts.encard seems fine to me, but maybe a notation O(G) would be nice to match V(G).

Snir Broshi said:

Also if you want to add defs/abbrevs for the order of a graph, I'd wait for the vertex-sets refactor, since I don't think it makes sense to define something on G : SimpleGraph V which only depends on V.
I'm not sure we should have defs/abbrevs since G.verts.ncard/G.verts.encard seems fine to me, but maybe a notation O(G) would be nice to match V(G).

Notation would also be very good. I personally like v(G) and e(G) in papers to match V(G) and E(G).

I don't think there is much advantage to to consolidating as notation / def / abbrev in terms of shortening any code or providing abstracted API (at least not at the current state of SimpleGraph). But I think a more naturally readable code and a consolidated reference (so any future architecture changes don't need to grep a bunch of different terms to find out all places where people are referencing the order or size of a graph) are both a plus.
And agreed that this doesn't have any urgency and should wait for the refactor (or be part of it).
